1.2.title: Electrical solver
1.2.description: Implement the lumped electrical model from docs/brief.md Section 6: sources, loads as current draws, per-net voltage, a battery whose capacity falls with draw, short-circuit detection. 1.3.title: Behaviour runtime

No part behaviour may be hard-coded in this package. Honour CLAUDE.md ground rules 1–14 (parts are data; sim-core pure and deterministic; real component names; no mascot/points/dialogs; touch + pointer + list-view paths together).

1.4.done_when: A two-motor robot drives straight, turns on the spot when one motor reverses, stops at a wall, and tips with the top-heavy fixture; tests pass.

decision_queue.question: Level 2 motor driver without a microcontroller: how is it commanded? (schema README Q1)
decision_queue.recommendation: Per-channel forward / stop / backward settings unlocked at Level 2; from Level 3 a driven signal overrides the setting. Build proceeds on this.

decision_queue.question: Level 3 servo: how does its angle setting relate to its signal input, and does the no-op brain pass the setting through? (schema README Q2; needed by 1.6 and 6.6)
decision_queue.recommendation: The servo turns to its angle setting only while a signal source drives its command input; the no-op brain's signal out carries the servo's setting through, so task 6.6's flag-on servo sweeps; no signal means hold and hum.

decision_queue.question: 'Low voltage: battery drains faster' measured against what? (schema README Q3)
decision_queue.recommendation: Per unit of motion: speed falls with voltage but current for the same load does not, so the pack drains more per wheel turn. Behaviour fixtures assert drain per revolution.

decision_queue.question: Switch (and other Level 1 parts) need a second failure mode for task 2.1's 'at least two each' (schema README Q4)
decision_queue.recommendation: Resolved in the 0.2 review: add the smallest additive need kind or effect before G0 freezes the schema, rather than relax 2.1's acceptance line.

decision_queue.question: Do unmounted parts ride along in a Run, and what happens at a floor edge with no wall? (schema README Q5; task 1.4)
decision_queue.recommendation: Unmounted parts stay where they were placed (their wires keep conducting, and a part with a mount need shows its mount fault); the floor boundary acts as a wall so the robot bumps and stops rather than leaving the arena.

decision_queue.question: Socket shapes: power round, signal square, mechanical hexagon (taken from the brief's listing order). Correct? (schema README Q6)
decision_queue.recommendation: Accept: power round, signal square, mechanical hexagon, paired with solid, dashed and thick grey line styles.

decision_queue.question: The child-written blueprint name travels with adult-to-adult sharing; a name could contain a child's first name. Acceptable? (schema README Q7; task 5.6)

decision_queue.question: Banned-words list vs 'mount point', a real term: how should 'points' be banned? (schema README Q8; task 2.5)

decision_queue.question: Level 1 motors: should two DC motors wired red-to-red on the chassis's left and right mounts drive the robot forward? Physically, mirror-mounted motors turn opposite ways unless one is rewired.
decision_queue.recommendation: Yes: the brief introduces polarity at Level 2, so Level 1 must not hinge on it. The chassis's motor mounts carry opposite handedness so red-to-red drives forward on both sides; swapping one motor's wires spins the robot (the Level 2 breakdown).

decision_queue.question: Brief Section 4 calls 'a motor straight off a brain's signal pin' legal-but-wrong, but also says a power wire into a signal port is refused. The schema resolves this with a red, current-limited 3V pin on the microcontroller; a yellow signal pin can never take a motor.
decision_queue.recommendation: Accept the red 3V pin: the Level 3 lesson (a brain cannot power a motor) survives and the socket rule stays simple.

decision_queue.question: Hint ladders: may a challenge's ladder skip a rung (for example no ghost wire when the fix is a setting, not a wire)? Brief Section 10 lists four rungs.
decision_queue.recommendation: Allow skipping only a rung that cannot apply to the fix; order is kept and every ladder ends with 'do it for me'.

decision_queue.question: Plan task 4.7 puts 'Cross the arena and stop at the wall' as the Level 1 unscripted build, but brief Section 5 shows it as the Level 2 example, and a Level 1 kit has no bumper switch to stop at a wall.

decision_queue.question: Under D23 the app's chassis mounts are mirrored so red-to-red drives forward, but in a real kit one motor's leads must be crossed. The parts-list export (task 5.3) has to bridge that gap.

decision_queue.question: Where does the adult (parent) view live, and how is it kept out of a child's way? (task 0.4 open question; tasks 5.1–5.4)

decision_queue.question: Gearbox lesson: a ramp preset at about 20 degrees (narrow window, clearance and tipping risks), or a heavy prop the bare motor cannot push? (R-2.2 Q4, D33, D46)

decision_queue.question: Circuit Crew (Level 2) kit contents: brief Section 5 lists battery pack, switch, 2 DC motors, motor driver, 2 wheels, caster, LED, buzzer; the Level 2 roster also has the 1-cell pack, gearbox, bumper switch, small wheel and servo motor.

decision_queue.question: Level 3 signal mappings chosen in task 1.3: a signal level (0 to 1) maps linearly onto a servo's angle range and onto a motor driver channel's command range. Confirm or replace in the Level 3 design.
decision_queue.recommendation: Accept the linear mappings for v1; revisit with the Level 3 design (brief Section 15, sub-draft 6). Levels 1–2 never produce a signal (D41), so nothing a tester sees depends on them.

decision_queue.question: Canvas rendering defaults chosen in task 3.1 (all in packages/canvas/docs/renderer.md): 2.5 px per mm at zoom 1; power and signal sockets side by side on a part's back edge; tiles at least 96 px or larger to fit their sockets; mount points drawn on the chassis under the parts on them; a mirrored picture's light ends up bottom-left; trackpad scroll zooms rather than pans; which fonts ship.
decision_queue.recommendation: Accept these as the defaults and settle them in the canvas interaction spec (brief Section 15, sub-draft 2) and the art style sheet; ship one rounded open-licence sans-serif (brief Section 11) once Drew names it.

decision_queue.question: Battery model (task 1.2): open-circuit volts fall in a straight line from volts to emptyVolts as charge is used, cutting off at empty, so a shorted pack empties in 35.0 s (1-cell) and 23.4 s (2-cell) rather than the constant-current 28.8 s and 19.2 s; a drained pack gives nothing; current either way drains a pack.
decision_queue.recommendation: Accept: it follows the schema's source definition and keeps the short's drain visible within half a minute; the capacity is a teaching value, not a real one.

decision_queue.question: Motor driver brown-out (task 1.2): when its supply sags below onVolts, it stutters at the duty that holds its supply at onVolts, so its motors turn slowly while the driver shows its own low-voltage; the alternative is that it cuts out.
decision_queue.recommendation: Accept the stutter (motors slow, driver shows low-voltage); it is the honest average of a real driver resetting under load and keeps the cause visible.

decision_queue.question: Servo motor draw and stall (tasks 1.2, 1.3): draw rises with load from idleMilliamps to stallMilliamps at holdingTorqueNmm, and the arm stalls at holdingTorqueNmm × volts ÷ ratedVolts; the record states neither.
decision_queue.recommendation: Accept both for v1; the Level 4 spec line and the behaviour-rules sub-draft (brief Section 15, item 4) confirm them with a robotics teacher.

decision_queue.question: D54 wording correction (review R-1.3): in the v1 runtime a signal level drives a motor driver channel forward only (0 to 1 maps onto 0 to full forward); reversing from a signal is not modelled.
decision_queue.recommendation: Accept forward-only for v1; the Level 3 design decides whether a signal can reverse a channel.

decision_queue.question: Mechanical defaults from task 1.4: a ramp's drop-off edge acts as a wall; wheel grip is the wheel's grip times the arena floor's friction; an unpowered DC motor brakes its wheel (a gear motor's gearbox resists turning); loose parts do not collide with the robot; hitting a wall never tips a robot; a fallen robot's wheels show no 'lifted' fault.
decision_queue.recommendation: Accept all six for Levels 1–2; revisit with the behaviour-rules sub-draft (brief Section 15, item 4) and a robotics teacher.

decision_queue.question: No Level 1–2 build can tip over with the real part records: a search of 2,152,008 builds found none on flat floor (caster-less builds settle on the frame at least 76 mm inside the edge), and on a slope tipping starts only at 49.7 degrees (the ramp preset is 8.1). Brief Sections 2–3 place 'balance a chassis' at Level 4. The plan's 2.6 fault list and 1.4's acceptance name a top-heavy tip.
decision_queue.recommendation: At Levels 1–2 the balance lesson is 'frame on the floor: the robot drags' (the 2.6 fixture broken-chassis-on-the-floor); true tipping is a Level 4 lesson with taller structures. The mechanical solver's tip is proven on a tall test variant.

decision_queue.question: Loose support attribution (review R-2.6 Q2, built into task 1.4): when a frame drags because the caster is loose, only the caster records a fault (mount · absent → drag); the chassis records no balance fault of its own. With no caster in the build at all, the chassis's own grounded/scraping fault applies.
decision_queue.recommendation: Accept: one fault, on the part the child must fix.

decision_queue.question: D61 figures corrected (review R-2.6 N1): without a caster, the most front-heavy Level 1–2 load reaches 34.2 mm (not 30.9) against the 40 mm axle, and tips on a slope only from 47.9 degrees (not 49.7); the conclusion stands: no Level 1–2 build tips.
decision_queue.recommendation: No change to D61's recommendation; the figures in its question were for the build with a caster.

decision_queue.question: Gate G2 sign-off (provisionally closed so the build continues): Drew reads every Level 1–2 spec card in docs/gates/G2.md (14 parts, every card line, hint and teaching note) and marks any change.
decision_queue.recommendation: Read docs/gates/G2.md; tick the sign-off box with the date; any line to change becomes a content fix task. Nothing technical waits on this.

decision_queue.question: D55 updated (review R-3.1): the canvas renderer's default choices are now the ten listed in packages/canvas/docs/renderer.md (scale, socket layout, tile sizes, mount-point drawing, mirrored light, trackpad zoom, fonts and three more). Known issue for task 3.3: sockets of neighbouring parts overlap on the Level 2 bumper robot and the Circuit Crew kit robot (5.6 px apart).
decision_queue.recommendation: Review renderer.md's ten choices with the canvas interaction spec; task 3.3 fixes the socket overlap before G3.

decision_queue.question: Edge panels and the 70% rule (task 4.1): holding the canvas to 70% with every edge beside it left the spec card 153–246 px wide. Brief Section 11 describes panels 'with soft shadows only where they overlap the canvas'.
decision_queue.recommendation: Panels may overlap the canvas edge with a soft shadow; at most 30% of the canvas is ever covered; the spec card is about 300–340 px wide where the screen allows; it never covers a port the child is wiring.

decision_queue.question: The Run bar: brief Section 9's table says 'always visible', but the same section says each edge can be tucked away. (task 4.1 Q2)
decision_queue.recommendation: The Run bar never tucks: Run/Stop is the one control a child must always reach; the tray, spec card, header and arena strip tuck.

decision_queue.question: Arena strip content and Home: no plan task owns the arena strip's preset picker and prop palette, or the Home screen (start a sandbox build, open saved builds, pick a challenge by level). (task 4.1 Q3)
decision_queue.recommendation: Task 4.5 (challenge runner) adds the arena strip's preset picker and prop palette (Build mode only, D36) and a minimal Home: sandbox, saved builds (from 4.9), and challenges by level.

decision_queue.question: Canvas placement details (review R-3.2): (1) a Move handle gives tap-then-tap moving, as the canvas docs promise for every drag; (2) a part held by a mount or shaft has no rotate handle, because its mount sets its orientation, and the card says to move it off to turn it; (3) turning by drag snaps to quarter turns like tap and the list view; (4) a removal says 'Removed with it: 2 wires' plus any loose parts' names; (5) free mount points under a placed part are still offered for now.
decision_queue.recommendation: Accept all five for G3; revisit (5) with the chassis content and the canvas interaction spec.

decision_queue.question: App shell details (review R-4.1): (1) the Run/Stop bar stays put between Build and Run; (2) the arena strip is part of the canvas, while the zoom control and tabs count as covering it; (3) the spec card may scroll within its 30% budget, and Level 1–2 cards aim to fit without scrolling at 10 inches; (4) the canvas takes safe-area insets so load and Fit centre the build in the uncovered area (task 3.7); (5) the spec card is hidden at rest and slides in when a part is selected.
decision_queue.recommendation: Accept all five for G3; settle the exact card height budget in the canvas interaction spec.

decision_queue.question: Saving and profiles before accounts exist (task 4.9): should every edit save, and what happens when no child profile exists yet?
decision_queue.recommendation: Autosave the current build about 1 s after the last edit and when Run is pressed (brief principle 5, nothing is lost); on first run create one local child profile with a neutral default name ('Builder 1'), which the parent view renames later; no email or personal data.

decision_queue.question: Release pipeline details (task 6.3): when does the content semver bump; should a deploy refuse a tester build without an invite-code seed; when should the app load a content bundle at run time instead of the one built in; should Settings be reached from Home behind the parental gate (D28, D68); should final art travel in the content bundle (D6)?
decision_queue.recommendation: Bump the content minor version for new records and the patch for text fixes (the hash suffix already identifies every bundle); refuse deploys of tester builds without a seed; keep the built-in content until a host exists, then add run-time bundle loading; Settings sits behind the parental gate on Home; art ships with the app until D6 is decided.

decision_queue.question: Store behaviour details (task 4.9, review R-4.9): status lines 'Not saved', 'Saved', 'Saved, and the other version kept as a copy', 'Builds are not being kept on this device'; 'Saved' appears only after Save is pressed; removing a build keeps its Runs as the child's progress; a profile with no loadable build starts an empty 'Build 1' on open floor.
decision_queue.recommendation: Accept for testers; task 6.5's copy pass reviews the status wording; removing a build keeping its Runs stays (progress is the child's).

decision_queue.question: Fault debounce (task 1.5): one-tick faults appeared at start-up (a driver brown-out), on heavy contact (a wheel slip) and after a bumper stop (a re-close). Should a fault need a minimum duration before it counts?
decision_queue.recommendation: Yes: a fault is recorded (and shown as a fault) only after 3 consecutive ticks (0.1 s), and ends after 3 ticks absent; live motion and values still show every tick as it is.

decision_queue.question: D31 'fixed': sim-core lists blueprint differences between two Runs that touch the faulted part, its ports or its wires (a wire removed and put back counts as no change). Accept this reading?
decision_queue.recommendation: Accept as built (R-1.5 Q1)

decision_queue.question: Should 'fixed' also count changes to the part that fed or explained the fault (e.g. browned-out driver fixed by a bigger battery pack)?
decision_queue.recommendation: No: D31 as written, only the faulted part, its ports and wires (R-1.5 Q2)

decision_queue.question: Debounced faults (D74): firstTick and the start event land on the 3rd active tick, shifting time-to-fix by 0.07 s. Keep?
decision_queue.recommendation: Keep as built (R-1.5 Q3)

decision_queue.question: Should golden runs also pin wire flows (canvas moving dots and flow labels)? A change reversing all power-line flows passes every check today.

decision_queue.question: Circuit Crew kit robot: bumper re-closes for one tick at tick 172 after stopping at the wall (LED, buzzer and motors on for 1/30 s). Accept at G1?
